title: Vision models often encoded the same concept change differently across contexts
summary: Across 46 vision encoders, the direction for a change such as dry to wet was detectable within individual visual contexts much more often than across them: 97.8% versus 18.3% of the compared cases in that example. The contrast varied substantially by concept.
ai_technology: Pretrained vision encoders including ViT; learned embedding representations and fitted probes

evidence.tested: The authors matched image embeddings for ten concept families, then compared within-context and cross-context direction consistency against random baselines. They also tested linear probe transfer across contexts.
evidence.unknown: Matching approximates changes in one concept using images that may differ in other ways. Detection rates depend on the chosen concepts, contexts, models, direction metric and statistical controls.
evidence.ai_role: Learned vision embeddings supplied concept-transition vectors for within- and cross-context tests, and fitted probes tested whether aligned directions predicted transfer.
